_comment: Shipping rates per product profile and destination.
Every variant in content/shop/*.md names a shippingProfile. A cart may
mix profiles (stickers plus a print, say); the customer is then charged the
HIGHEST applicable rate once, not the sum, because the order ships together.
Country codes are matched first. _EUROPE catches the remaining countries in
the europe list below, _WORLD catches everything else.
After editing, run:  node scripts/sync-worker-config.mjs
then:                cd checkout-worker && npx wrangler deploy
No Stripe key needed - rates are created inline per checkout, so nothing
has to be registered in the Stripe dashboard.
Google Merchant Center follows on its own: on every push to main that
touches this file, .github/workflows/merchant-shipping.yml runs
scripts/sync-merchant-shipping.mjs, which rewrites the shipping policies in
Merchant Center from this table. Each profile name is the shipping_label
the product feed puts on its variants. Do not edit the policies by hand in
Merchant Center; the next sync replaces them.
handlingDays is how long an order waits to be made before it ships.
taxCode txcd_92010001 is Stripe's 'Shipping' code, so Stripe Tax applies the
right rate to postage rather than guessing.
shipTo lists every country checkout offers, as code → name, kept to the
markets we sell to on purpose. Because of the EU Packaging and Packaging
Waste Regulation (PPWR) we currently do not ship to the EU/EEA. The cart
dropdown is built from this list (src/lib/countries.ts), the Worker refuses
any country that is not on it, and Merchant Center gets a shipping policy
for each of them. Anyone else can join the waitlist on a product page.
